column2: With our department having approximately 130 individual services, this new process has been extremely time-consuming, taxing, and frustrating.  The template is very finicky and required many additional hours for data entry as we could not simply copy and paste from previous or existing in-house workbooks. The process for requesting new SIDs and STIDs was laborious and frustrating, certainly not easy or accurate.  We also spent many additional hours correcting system-generated errors when it issued (sometimes repeatedly) false or duplicate SIDs or STDs. This new process has also caused a rift in collaboration between the Service and Security divisions within our department who now must work separately to complete similar work related to critical services and the Service Inventory.  In discussions with our Security counterparts, their side of the service inventory work (critical services) lacks support and clear direction -- our colleagues leaned heavily on our Service team to provide guidance and training on how to use GCEPM (formerly used for Service Inventory as Clarity) as they felt they did not receive adequate training or direction from TBS Security section. This has added additional stress to our Service workload that should be innovative instead of regressive in both process and reporting tools. The messaging and direction to our two divisions varied and caused a lot of confusion within the department. The Clarity tool and former reporting process is favoured by our team in comparison to the most recent year's.

This year was the best for availability from the service team, including quick email responses, replies to GCxchange messages, and clear answers from the drop in sessions. I have been the lead for 4 years now and this year was by far the best in customer service and having clear instructions.

I like the changes but it all happened at once and also the data crossing and the fixes required several contacts with the branches and not all people were inclined to provide information in the allowed period so we couldn't provide a whole and fixed information because of the deadlines. Having more time to prepare and to provide feedback in the requests is important for both sides, but i understand this was the first year and the start in the new process, so it is all undesttandable.

More help was needed when defining what a service means in the context of the department as SSC's clients are other government departments and not citizens. Not all services offered by SSC could be considered directly orderable or consumable. Clearer instructions when reporting service standards (or lack of data) ahead of time would have been helpful.

The Excel template is not easy to use and instructions were sparse.  I recommend using an online portal to capture information rather than trying to fit our requirements into an Excel spreadsheet. Also, macros are disabled in our organization, so it was challenging for us to use the spreadsheet.
I'd like to enhance the communication with TBS for guidance and clarifications.

Gregory et Francesca ont toujours répondu rapidement à mes questions. Gregory a été disponible pour des rencontres individuelles pour m'aider à trouver les informations recherchées et me soutenir dans la génération des codes de programme. Un grand merci de votre soutien.

Reporting of errors was very challenging. We were told we had critical errors, but then did not. This can create a lot of problems up the reporting chain. Definitions are unclear. Should have more clearly indicated the relationship between program codes and departments. In the Excel spreadsheet, it’s just one long list, so if you were unaware, you wouldn’t know that the codes are department-specific. For example, we associated the code BY103 (Public Education and Information) with our Public Enquiries service, but it turned out that the code is specific to the Office of the Chief Electoral Officer. While their website makes this clear, it’s not as evident in the definitions section of the Excel spreadsheet.

The fact that the service inventory team (besides Gregory Erikson, he has exceptional client service) point people to GC Connex, or links, or whatever rather than answering questions is  a constant irritant, year over year. It's quite terrible.
Conflicting information and process regarding Service Inventory data requirements and Critical Services requirements continues to be a challenge.

The process seems to be designed for tangible services and it is difficult to apply it to grants and scholarships.  Furthermore, the information is provided in November but it takes months to see it on gcinfobase.  Any correction to be made is then difficult and complicated.

Process used to communicate critical errors was very confusing and created panic at senior management levels. Minor errors should not have been included especially when these can not be addressed at this time.  Titan was the preferred portal for data entry as it was easy to use and errors were communicated immediately through the portal.

Not ideal that departments had to correct errors in service ID assignments caused by TBS after they had submitted their Service Inventory for 2023-2024. Also, it was difficult to get a response from the Service Policy inbox on what the best path forward was for addressing a data display error for service data on Infobase. On other issues, they were very responsive.
Confusion with Critical Service and Non-critical services. To clarify the two reporting requirements or integrate them.
Consistency of information related to GC Service Inventory does not always occur. Attempts to stay ahead of process is hard because of the constant changes in Service inventory process.
Thank you for the opportunity to provide feedback. We did incorporate some of the design elements from your excel template into our internal reports.

I think a debrief session with all participating departments could be worthwhile. Each penholder for their department can express what worked well and what did not. The survey won't capture the finer details.

For example, in our case there were numerous problems with the portal and the template because the character limit between English and French were identical. This prevented us from uploading or deleting our entries for quite some time.

Instructions need to be more clear... There is no reference document or support materials to refer to. Very vague process which makes it difficult for someone to do this process for the first time, with no background whatsoever.

Any changes to data collection/ needs must be communicated officially from TBS prior to the data collection time period, it is not sufficient to "mention it in a workshop" and then implement the changes. Clear instructions as to how Deputy Head approval will be collected should be given, forwarding an email is not ideal. Any data definitions must be clearly defined prior to the collection period in order to maintain governance, being informed that there are new relational components after submission of the inventory is not sufficient.
I appreciated the drop-in sessions. Extremely helpful. Instructions pertaining to the IDs and what to include was not clear; however, easily rectified through the drop in sessions.

Being the first time my unit to conduct the Service inventory on behalf of WAGE, it required transfer of knowledge  that took extra work and time.  As mention higher up , the understanding of the definition was sometime challenging, the support given by TBS was required and appreciated.

There has been a different submission process every year for the past three years (e.g., Excel spreadsheet submission by email, submission in Clarity only, Excel spreadsheet loaded to Open Gov Portal, etc.). It would be really helpful to establish a consistent process so that it becomes less burdensome, because very time the process changes, we have to devote additional hours to learn the new process, and then adapt our own internal processes. Key Areas for Consideration
1. Service Inventory Reporting Requirements
•	The introduction of new fields (e.g., ‘Automated Decision-Making’ and ‘Program ID Code’) brought some challenges in ensuring accurate completion.
•	Certain definitions, such as "Is the service supported by automated decision-making," could benefit from greater clarity to facilitate consistent interpretation across departments.
•	Multiple updates to reporting requirements this year necessitated repeated adjustments, resulting in a time-consuming and intensive process.
2. Service Inventory Process and the New Template
•	The new template was provided later than in previous years, which made it difficult to integrate into existing workflows.
•	Mid-cycle modifications to the template resulted in inconsistencies and required additional rework.
•	The template’s format, particularly the lack of pre-populated data, increased manual effort and complexity.
•	Given these challenges, ESDC had to rely on its previous template and manually align the data, which significantly increased workload.
•	We don’t think that backlogs information should have been removed from the template.
•	We don’t think that the last year for review of service standards should have been removed from the template. 
3. Transition to the Open Government Portal
•	While the transition was intended to streamline the process, it introduced additional complexity, requiring time and technical knowledge to navigate.
•	Questions related to registration and account setup had to be addressed by a separate TBS team, which led to confusion.
•	A technical issue caused by the transition to Open Gov prevented our Inventory from being uploaded by the November 30 deadline, putting our submission at risk.
•	There should have been more testing with departments or a pilot. 
4. TBS List of Reporting Issues (critical and minor)
•	Many of the flagged errors stemmed from the limitations of the quality control script, which does not account for contextual explanations provided in non-standard responses.
•	Of the 29 reporting issues ESDC received, the majority were minor technical issues rather than substantive errors.
•	In some cases, flagged errors related to application volume reporting were not applicable to certain services, highlighting the need for a broader metric that captures the full scope of service interactions.
•	However, the most recent issue with Program ID codes reveled some errors in the Inventory that we were unaware of. Since the request to add a program ID code was new, and our templates were not pre-populated, we were unsure whether we had selected the correct program codes. It was only after receiving a message from TBS that we realized we had used the wrong ID code for a new service. As a result, we reached out to find a responsible Branch within ESDC to review and validate all program codes to identify any potential mistakes which, as it turned out, we had made.
To help improve the Service Inventory process in the future, we would like to share the following recommendations for your consideration:
•	Providing the Service Inventory reporting requirements and updated templates by May each year would allow departments sufficient time for adjustments and the implementation of new requirements.
•	The template should be pre-populated with previous submissions to minimize manual entry and the risk of errors. It should also allow for flexible data entry, including non-standard responses.
•	Departments should have sufficient time to test new platforms and templates before the final submission deadline. A pilot testing phase could help in identifying potential issues early.
•	The system should flag errors immediately during data entry would help prevent last-minute corrections.
•	TBS should reconsider the restriction of volumetric reporting to "applications" and introduce a broader metric that reflects the full scope of service delivery activities.
•	When transitioning from one platform or the system (e.g. GC EPM to Open Government Portal) a comprehensive training and guidance would help departments adapt efficiently.
We recognize the complexities involved in refining the Service Inventory process and appreciate the steps TBS has already taken to improve it. We hope these suggestions will contribute to a more streamlined and user-friendly experience moving forward.
Thank you for your time and consideration. We look forward to continued collaboration on these improvements.

The sooner we receive confirmation of any new or changed data fields related to the Service Inventory, the better prepared we are to start communicating with Service Management Representatives to gather their service area updates. Our team has been working to integrate the annual update into other reporting frameworks, so the more time we have, the better we can ensure alignment across all areas. Thanks to the Service Team at TBS for all their support.

There is very unclear expectations about service reporting for the future, including its exclusion from requirements for the upcoming DPSD. I have sent emails to the service and digital mailbox without response and have now included the service policy mailbox as well.

The data collection template caused the most frustration.  The color coding when entering data, for instance, made certain areas appear as 'not required' due to the dark coloring, which led to confusion.
Having been my first time completing the service inventory, it was extremely unclear from the beginning whether this was a reporting or a planning exercise.

Stakeholders/service owners most often see this exercise as a tick in the box and don't understand its importance, and we struggle explaining it to them. A few key messages around the "Why SIU and why it is important" would be helpful.

same as #question 13. Improve TBS processes, call out and please no last minute changes. No more call out in Sept. Get organized and have it sent out to us by no later than May. Get started now please. This experience needs to change and be better, it has been the same since 2020. Thank you.

1) Conflicting messages between instructions received via email and on the portal and the messages we received during the drop-in sessions; 2) lack of awareness that a zero value IS a value; 3) there was a bug in the template that we had to first identify and then "fix" - upload of a single document impossible; had to manually enter one service - after which the rest of the services could be uploaded.   Fortunately I drew heavily on my experience using the OGP for consultations and was able to resolve 4) receiving notifications that some aspects of our submission were "incorrect" EVEN THOUGH they were verified and accepted by OGP program the week before most Deputy Heads took off for the Christmas break was very frustrating - especially when we still didn't receive clarity during a Dec. 16th meeting

We need to be informed way earlier in the process when changes are coming so we can adequately prepare ourselves and non- service colleagues who will be involved in the NEW process. The call letter should be sent in spring to allow more time and more realistic timeframe to complete the exercise and correct errors, if needed.

The process is better using the Open Government Portal though the Business Continuity Information that was removed and handle through the Security team did cause confusion.  More clear instruction on how to use the Portal and putting more user related information on the GC Exchange site.   Organize the structure of information on the GC Exchange site better so it can be found more easily.
No

As mentioned above, understanding the definitions of what was required in the data collection templates were a bit of a challenge, but the support provided by TBS was very helpful and much appreciated.
Two issues identified (minor) after submission in the portal.
some parts of the instructions were unclear, such as the need to email deputy head approval

Excel template was very difficult to use (coding not useful). Changing reporting portals every year is challenging.
Is there another tool other than excel that could be explored to collect and submit the data e.g. GC Forms?
Shift from EPM to excel template resulted in additional work to generate the spreadsheet

The integrated call letter should be released earlier. Data relationships should be clearly explained as they are applied in GCepm for GCapm and critical service information and how service information needs to be correlated to the critical applications listed in apm and on the CBAS list.  Future dashboards utilizing service information should be openly shared so all departments can give feedback.
Communication on the overall purpose of the reporting exercise; Changing requirements and definitions
There were a number of errors identified following submission, and it was not clear what the error related to or how to resolve them.

The format is not user friendly and so we felt compelled to put it in a different format to gather information from service leads across the organization and to seek approval from our Deputies on the substance of the update. We then manually converted the data back into the TBS template so we could do the upload. This adds extra effort and time to the process.
While not 'tight timelines' modifying the template throughout the process, caused major delays.

follow up on "critical issues" with service inventory was very confusing, far too many emails, raising alarms about not significant issues and lack of common sense and judgment around what was actually meant to be reported and achieved with the process.
I feel an FAQ could have helped answer many questions. Maybe a quick video (CSPS training style video) could easily explain all about this particular exercise.

TBS call out are coming way too late in the process (around mid-end of Sept) and requiring DM approval a months later and data entry 7 weeks after. The call out comes with surprises with unexpected changes which messes up with current internal call out. Deadline are too tight, and changes of requirements are communicated too late. Solution: 1. Have call out ready by latest May with clear requirements and deadlines. 2. Maintain Drop in sessions throughout the summer. It is frustrating getting TBS call out in Sept, this has been happening since 2020, could we improve process please. It will facilitate our work. Also call out keep changing from one year to another, we are ok with that but then again finalize it by May and then no mroe last minute change like we have experiences last time (some columns were removed and we needed to add two more... unacceptable request, unrealistic and disrepectful). Please consider impact on any changes or last minute changes on departments and agencies. Respect the fact that we need at least 5 months to get a request like this to be completed on our end.
The error messages and some definitions in the file aren't clear with providing details on how to make corrections on your own. Not intuitive
